Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And at every period of seven years you shall perform a release.
translations.2: And this is the explanation of the release: that every holder of a loan shall release his hand from what he demands of his fellow — he shall not press his fellow nor his brother, since it has already been called a release unto God.
translations.3: As for the stranger, it is permitted that you press him; but what belongs to you from your brother — release your hand from it.
translations.4: And it is certain that there shall be no poor person among you — inasmuch as God shall bless you in the land which He gives you as an inheritance to possess.
translations.5: So long as you continue to hear and accept the command of God your Lord, and to keep and act upon all this law which I command you today.
translations.6: Since God your Lord has already bestowed His blessing upon you, as He promised you — you shall supply the needs of many nations, while you shall not supply your need from them; and you shall have dominion over many of them, but they shall not have dominion over you.
translations.7: If there be among you a poor person, whether by reason of sin or of affliction, from among some of your brothers in some of your localities, in your land which God your Lord is giving you — do not harden your heart against him, nor close your hand from him.
translations.8: Rather, open it to him fully, and supply his need completely, according to the measure of what he lacks.
translations.9: Beware lest there be in your heart a word of ignorance, so that you say: 'The seventh year, the year of the release, has drawn near' — and you be miserly toward your poor brother and give him nothing; and he cry out against you to God, and a punishment befall you.
translations.10: Rather, give him a gift, and let not your soul be miserly toward him — for it is on account of this matter that God your Lord will bless you in your labors and in all that you put your hand to.
translations.11: For, as I have told you, the poor shall never cease from the land — and therefore I command you today that you open your hand to your brother, to your needy one and to your poor one in your land.
translations.12: And if your Hebrew brother or your Hebrew sister be sold to you, let him serve you six years; and in the seventh year, release him free from your presence.
translations.13: And when you release him free from your presence, do not release him empty-handed.
translations.14: Rather, provide him with a gift — from your flock, and your grain, and your produce — according to what God your Lord has provided you, you shall give him.
translations.15: And remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and God your Lord redeemed you — and therefore I command you this matter today.
translations.16: But if he says to you: 'I will not go out from your presence' — because he loves you and loves your household, since it is better for him to remain with you —
translations.17: then take the branding-iron and put it in his ear at your door, and he shall be your slave forever. And your maidservant likewise — do the same for her.
translations.18: And do not let it be hard for you to release him free from your presence, for it may well be that he has served you double the worth of a hired laborer's wage; and God your Lord will bless you in all that you do.
translations.19: Every firstborn that is born to you from your flock and your cattle — the male — bind upon it the consecration due to God your Lord. You shall not work the firstborn of your cattle, nor shear the firstborn of your flock.
translations.20: Rather, eat it before God your Lord, year by year, in the place which God shall choose — you and your household.
translations.21: But if there be a blemish in it — lameness or blindness, or any of the disqualifying blemishes — you shall not slaughter it for God your Lord.
translations.22: It is permitted that you eat it in your localities, and that the impure and the pure alike eat it, just as the meat of the gazelle and the deer is eaten.
translations.23: Except its blood — do not eat it; rather, pour it out upon the ground like water.
